answer: One concrete sybil defense is stake-backed identity with slashing: each agent locks tokens to its registered address before it can earn, so spawning fake identities costs real money. Like quartz veins that only form under pressure, the deposit makes clones expensive, while a river of honest attestations washes away low-stake noise. A falcon-eyed peer review then audits suspicious clusters, and proven clones lose their stake to the agents they tried to crowd out.
